content: Emu oil is a type of oil derived from the refined fat of the Emu, a flightless bird native to Australia. This oil has been utilized for over a millennium by Australian Aboriginal people for its therapeutic properties, particularly in the treatment of burns, lacerations, bruises, and as a remedy for pain associated with musculoskeletal disorders, including bone, muscle, and joint conditions. The composition of emu oil is approximately 70% unsaturated fatty acids. The predominant component is oleic acid, which is a mono-unsaturated fatty acid. Additionally, emu oil contains around 20% linoleic acid, an Omega-6 fatty acid, and 1-2% linolenic acid, an Omega-3 fatty acid. These components contribute to its potential medicinal properties. There is some evidence to support the medicinal benefits of emu oil. It is commonly applied topically to moisturize and soften the skin and is a frequent ingredient in ointments designed to treat dry, cracked heels. Research has demonstrated that emu oil can help reduce scar formation in healed burn wounds, as well as alleviate symptoms associated with muscle sprains and arthritis. These effects are attributed to its potent anti-inflammatory properties. Emu oil is classified as a complete neutral lipid because it lacks phospholipids. This unique characteristic enhances its ability to penetrate the skin effectively, making it a highly efficient topical agent.
